rules.body: Apply when deferred document saves outlive a view subscription and persistence can synchronously navigate. README.md: "A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge. Save callbacks can synchronously navigate." docs/host-api.md: "Document buffers are owned by the coordinator dictionary, while Badge owns only a live subscription." Keep the reusable save task in the coordinator dictionary, keyed by document identity; retiring a subscription must not destroy its document's pending text.

Route active-document edits through the existing trailing task with a 120 ms quiet interval. Reset the interval on additional edits, retain the latest text, and keep the task reusable after consumption. TASK: "Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet\ninterval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts\nmust continue to save." Bind the consumer to the buffer's document identity rather than looking up the current view when the timer fires.

Preserve the utility's detach-before-consume ordering so synchronous consumer reentry can enqueue another burst without outer cleanup erasing it. src/services.js: "const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };" Preserve valid empty text; do not replace the explicit pending-value check with a truthiness check.

Preserve pending document edits on open, close, and disposal by flushing the departing buffer rather than canceling its work. Complete that flush before departure returns as a preservation inference: TASK says "Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces." Original src/coordinator.js writes synchronously in "edit(text){const view=getView();if(view){env.store.write(view.id,text);}}" and docs/host-api.md states "Store read/write/subscribe is synchronous; timer schedule(callback,delay), cancel(handle) is explicitly controlled." Retire the departing live subscription separately from the coordinator-owned buffer.

Treat flushing as a synchronous reentry boundary. Publish departure state and complete old-view cleanup before invoking the save consumer, or guard subsequent effects against a newer navigation. Give each open or close a new request identity and recheck the outer open after departure before publishing its view. Audit workspace disposal cleanup too: outer cleanup must not erase a view installed by a save listener. docs/host-api.md: "A store listener may call navigation synchronously." README.md: "Save callbacks can synchronously navigate."

Preserve interfaces, document identities/text, and status payload semantics while changing save timing. docs/host-api.md: "All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics." Keep preview independent: TASK says "The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change." src/services.js: "const task = trailing(timers, 40, query => publish({query}));" and "return {query: text => task.push(text), hide: () => task.cancel()};" Do not transfer document flushing policy to preview hide.

Verify with controlled timers: no write before 120 ms of quiet; one latest-text write at expiration; another later burst saves; empty text saves; departure persists the original document's text before returning; reopening retains that text. Exercise save listeners that synchronously open another document or close, through both timer consumption and departure flushing, and verify outer navigation or disposal cleanup preserves the resulting authoritative state. Separately verify preview's existing 40 ms delay, hide cancellation, and reuse. These checks derive from the cited task and source behavior; evaluation observations add no requirements.

limitations: Departure flushing before return is a preservation inference from TASK and the original synchronous edit implementation, not an explicit timing requirement in TASK.
The sources do not prescribe exception recovery or behavior for calls after dispose.
Attempt 1 reports passing observations, but one passing implementation does not establish causality, exhaustive correctness, or benefit across tasks.
Apply the persistence rules to document buffers; transient work with a documented discard policy requires different boundary handling.

notes: Not approved; training acceptance or expert summary does not verify cross-task effectiveness
